record.body:
## Problem

The `Store` class is the only storage interface, and canon-internal code and a few modules outside it depend on its file layout. A second backend cannot land until a backend interface exists.

## Approach

Add a `Backend` protocol and `open_backend` factory. Make `Store` the file backend. Move validation, merge, sync, migrate and the CLI onto the protocol, and move the layout checks into the file backend. Fix the six outside touches. Settled by the user: the two backends coexist until cutover. Decision: `canon-backend-coexist`.

## Exit criteria

- R1 to R13 of the specification pass. Verified by the unit tests in `tests/canon` and the boundary test.
- `canon list --full` on the real store is identical before and after. Verified by a diff of the two outputs.
- The configured phase suite and `canon validate` pass. Verified by running them.

## Proof

kind: commands. A human runs the boundary test and the before/after diff of `canon list --full`, and sees no difference.

## Execution

Session shape: more than one. Execute the core backend boundary, then external consumers, then verification. Human stops: push and PR merge; automatic planning and dispatch authorized by the user. Collision notes: other efforts are active; code stays in isolated worktrees and only this session writes the primary store.

## Landing

Branch: phase/access-layer. Worktree: /home/andrewyin/orchestra/.worktrees/access-layer. Base: main. Commit task code, integrate into phase branch, run verification, review and configured suite, commit this effort's store records on the phase branch, push and open PR. Merge only with user approval and passing CI, using gh pr merge --squash. Do not merge locally into protected main. Subsequent phases may stack on verified phase heads pending landing approval.

payload.title: Route all store reads through orchestra.canon
